objective.statement: Map a re-litigated decision into an explicit argument graph, anchor every node to its transcript span, and find which leaf premise the decision actually rests on.
objective.charter: A decision that has been re-argued twice is usually not a disagreement about the conclusion - it is an undetected disagreement about one leaf premise that nobody has isolated. Three mappers build the graph: claims, the premises supporting them, and the evidence under those premises. Every node must carry the transcript span it came from, so the graph cannot contain a premise nobody actually asserted. Four claim adjudicators then rule premise by premise, and a sensitivity sweep flips each leaf premise in turn to find the ones that change the conclusion. Those, and only those, are worth re-arguing.
success_criteria: every graph node carries the transcript span it was extracted from
no node is a paraphrase nobody asserted - a node without a span is deleted, not repaired
a sensitivity sweep is run over every leaf premise
the report names the specific leaf premises whose truth value flips the conclusion

context.briefing: Extract claims verbatim with their span. If you cannot point at where it was said, it is not a node.
Flip each leaf premise in turn and record whether the conclusion moves. A premise nobody's conclusion depends on is not worth a third round of argument.

committees.mandate: Build the claim/premise/evidence graph. Every node carries its transcript span; a node without a span is deleted.
Rule premise by premise on the finished graph. You may not add nodes.

sequence.custom_name: P42 argument mapping: claims -> premises -> evidence, each node anchored to a transcript span
P15 claim-by-claim adjudication walked over the graph's leaf premises
flip each leaf premise and record whether the conclusion moves

all_of.producer: graph linter: counts nodes whose transcript span does not resolve, divided by total nodes, subtracted from 1
all_of.note: DIAL 1 of 3 - 'every node carries its transcript span'. Must be exactly 1. Lowering this admits paraphrases nobody asserted, which is the failure mode that makes a re-litigated decision unresolvable in the first place.

all_of.producer: sensitivity sweep: flips each leaf premise and records whether the conclusion changes
all_of.note: DIAL 2 of 3 - the design's minimum-deliberation floor. Without the sweep the council produces a pretty graph and no ranking of what matters.
DIAL 3 of 3 - every premise carries an explicit ruling. An unruled premise is exactly what gets re-litigated a third time.

conditional_decision_requires: the argument graph is attached, with the unanchored-node count stated (it must be zero)
the sensitivity table names which leaf premises flip the conclusion

metadata.title: Argument-map council (10 seats) - for a decision re-litigated twice
metadata.notes: WHEN TO USE: the design is explicit - invoke when a decision has been re-litigated TWICE. The second re-argument is the trigger, not the first. WHEN NOT TO USE: on a fresh decision (there is no transcript to anchor to, so every node fails the anchoring gate) or on an ideation question. The design's named dial is graph_depth. EDITABLE DIALS: /stopping/expression/all_of/0/value (anchoring ratio - keep at 1), /voting/score_scale (graph support strength), /participants/roster (mapper:adjudicator ratio, 3:4 here), /targets/evidence_items, /budgets/time_minutes. STOPPING (human form): custom:graph_nodes_anchored_ratio >= 1 AND custom:leaf_premise_sensitivity_run == true AND every_objection_addressed == true. source_expression absent per the collision proven by _probe_sem_rule_collision.py. PRESET-NAME: `custom` with extends_preset root_cause_council. Argument mapping has no counterpart among the 24 required preset names; root_cause_council is the nearest (it also isolates a cause) but is claimed by the ACH preset in another lane, and evidence_adjudication_jury is claimed by C-D42. Declaring `custom` rather than mislabelling was the deliberate choice.
